record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: Which compact subsets K of the complex plane can occur as the spectrum σ(T) of a frequently hypercyclic operator T acting on a complex Banach space?

evidence.quote:
Problem 5. Which compact subsets of C can be the spectrum of a frequently hypercyclic
operator on a complex Banach space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a complex separable infinite-dimensional Banach space and let T : X → X be a bounded linear operator. The operator T is called frequently hypercyclic if there exists a vector x ∈ X (called a frequently hypercyclic vector) such that, for every nonempty open subset U ⊆ X, the set N(x,U) = { n ∈ ℕ : T^n x ∈ U } has positive lower density, i.e.

  liminf_{N→∞} (1/N) #{ n ≤ N : T^n x ∈ U } > 0.

Denote by σ(T) ⊆ ℂ the spectrum of T. 

Characterize precisely those nonempty compact subsets K ⊆ ℂ that arise as K = σ(T) for some frequently hypercyclic operator T on some complex Banach space X. Equivalently, give necessary and sufficient conditions on a compact set K ⊆ ℂ so that there exists a complex Banach space X and a frequently hypercyclic bounded linear operator T : X → X with σ(T) = K.
artifact.status_search_result: A full characterization is not known. A known necessary condition is that the spectrum of a frequently hypercyclic operator on a complex Banach space has no isolated points (Shkarin, 2012, arXiv:1209.1221); this in particular implies non-existence of frequently hypercyclic operators on complex hereditarily indecomposable Banach spaces. However, a complete description of which perfect compact subsets of ℂ actually occur as spectra of frequently hypercyclic operators has not been established in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: On the spectrum of frequently hypercyclic operators
status_evidence.snippet: The spectrum of a frequently hypercyclic operator has no isolated points; consequently no frequently hypercyclic operators exist on complex hereditarily indecomposable Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a necessary condition (no isolated points) but not a full characterization.

status_evidence.title: On the spectrum of supercyclic/hypercyclic operators
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses which compact sets can occur as spectra of hypercyclic/supercyclic operators; the analogous question for frequently hypercyclic operators remains without a complete answer.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses related spectral questions but does not give a full characterization in the frequently hypercyclic case.
